title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 Flow Control Architecture
purpose: Map RFC 9250 section 5.8 flow control requirements to the shared QUIC transport runtime and remembered-parameter policy without adding a custom DoQ flow-control layer.
design_summary: DoQ relies on the shared QUIC transport runtime for all flow-control behavior. Connection-wide receive limits map to `InitialMaxData` and the runtime's connection receive window, per-stream receive limits map to the `InitialMaxStreamData*` transport parameters and per-stream receive limits in `QuicConnectionStreamState`, stream creation limits map to `InitialMaxStreamsBidi` and `InitialMaxStreamsUni`, and 0-RTT reuse is governed by remembered transport parameters. The runtime's handshake commit path applies the peer transport-parameter values into the stream registry bookkeeping. The adapter stays thin and does not add its own credit accounting or backpressure layer.
data_and_state_considerations: All limit tracking stays inside `QuicConnectionStreamState`, `QuicConnectionRuntime.Protocol.cs`, the transport parameter codec, and the zero-RTT remembered-parameter policy. DoQ only forwards option values into the transport runtime and relies on the runtime to surface `DATA_BLOCKED`, `STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED`, `STREAMS_BLOCKED`, `FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR`, and `STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR` outcomes where appropriate.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Client-initiated bidirectional query streams must be permitted by the server-side peer stream limit before DoQ traffic can flow.
Locally initiated bidirectional responses are governed by the client's own receive window for that stream, not by the peer-initiated stream limit.
0-RTT acceptance must compare remembered initial flow-control limits against the current server limits and reject any reduction in the required values.
risks: If callers leave the server-side stream limits at a base `QuicConnectionOptions` default, DoQ will not be able to accept queries.
Changing the transport runtime's flow-control semantics would affect all protocols that share the QUIC layer, not just DoQ.

supplemental_sections.heading: Flow-Control Mapping
supplemental_sections.content: Aggregate connection receive limits come from `InitialMaxData` and the runtime's `ConnectionReceiveLimit`. Per-stream receive limits come from `InitialMaxStreamDataBidiLocal`, `InitialMaxStreamDataBidiRemote`, and `InitialMaxStreamDataUni`, which the runtime stores as the receive limit for the corresponding stream direction. Stream creation limits come from `InitialMaxStreamsBidi` and `InitialMaxStreamsUni`, which gate `TryOpenLocalStream` and peer-initiated stream admission. The handshake commit path in `QuicConnectionRuntime.Protocol.cs` applies the received transport parameters into the bookkeeping limits that enforce these ceilings. 0-RTT uses remembered transport parameters so the first connection's flow-control floor continues to control resumed early data.
